newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FOCUS-BHP shares touch two-year low.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FOCUS-BHP shares touch two-year low.

text.p: Australia's largest company, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, on Thursday saw its shares touch a two-year low in a sustained sell-off which has so far wiped over A$1.5 billion (US$1.2 billion) off their market value this week.

The Australian steel, energy and minerals giant, the world's second biggest producer of copper, was battered for a third straight day on the Australian stock market as copper prices continued to fall, analysts said.
BHP's share price breached a previous 1996 low of A$15.90 and continued tumbling to a low of A$15.58 in afternoon trade, its lowest ebb since May 1994.
"There just seems to be a bit of nervousness in resources (stocks) in general. It's not just BHP," J.B. Were and Son analyst Neil Goodwill told Reuters.
A Sydney-based analyst said there was no reason why BHP shares could not fall further, based on the stock's share price to earnings (PE) ratio.
"It's on a PE of 19 or 20. People usually pay a PE multiple of that amount for growth stocks," he said, adding BHP was not a growth stock at the moment.
"So I think it can go down a lot more ... it is very rapidly losing its lead over other companies."
It recovered to close at A$16, down 93 cents or five percent since Monday's close.
BHP represents about 10 percent of the overall Australian share market, which ended 9.7 points or 0.43 percent lower on Thursday against Wednesday's close.
The stock's descent reflects concern at the impact of weak copper and steel prices on BHP and profit downgrades issued by a few major brokerages, analysts and brokers told Reuters.
Analyst Keith Williams, of BT Securities, agreed the slide could continue.
"I think the absolute downside would be A$15 and then people would just declare that it is ridiculously cheap," he said.
But analyst Tim Gerard of Prudential Bache said the share price appeared to have bottomed out.
"But when the market gets in a mood like this, you just never know how low it is going to go," he added.
"If Asia turns around and goes from being average to going worse in terms of minerals demand and America sags a little bit then BHP will keep going lower."

"For the next week there will be further concern until I think you see that earnings number out," a market source said, referring to BHP's scheduled release on September 20 of its profit results for its first fiscal quarter ending August.
The announcement will be BHP's first issue of results since it posted in June a 14 percent slump in group net profit after abnormals in the year to May 31.
The stock's slide on Thursday coincided with a sharp fall in copper prices in Asian futures trading.
